exam_set.title: Practice Set 4
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 3, Practice Set 4

questions.jp: 再帰呼び出しの説明はどれか。
questions.romaji: Saiki yobidashi no setsumei wa dore ka.

options.label: ア
options.jp: あらかじめ決められた順番ではなく、起きた事象に応じた処理を行うこと
options.romaji: Arakajime kimerareta junban dewa naku, okita jishō ni ōjita shori o okonau koto

options.label: イ
options.jp: 関数の中で自分自身を用いた処理を行うこと
options.romaji: Kansū no naka de jibun jishin o mochiita shori o okonau koto
options.en: A function performs processing using itself.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 処理が終了した関数をメモリから消去せず、必要になったとき再び用いること
options.romaji: Shori ga shūryō shita kansū o memorī kara shōkyo sezu, hitsuyō ni natta toki futatabi mochiiru koto

options.label: エ
options.jp: 処理に失敗したときに、その処理を呼び出す直前の状態に戻すこと
options.romaji: Shori ni shippai shita toki ni, yobidasu chokuzen no jōtai ni modosu koto
options.en: Restore state before a failed call.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Recursion happens when a function asks itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem. For example, “count down from 3” can print 3 and ask the same function to count down from 2. A base case, such as stopping at 0, prevents the self-calls from continuing forever.

Technical breakdown:
A recursive function contains a call to itself, normally with an argument that moves toward a base case. The call creates another invocation; after the deepest invocation finishes, results return through the earlier calls. The defining clue is not repetition alone, but a function or procedure invoking itself.

Japanese keywords to remember:
再帰 = saiki = recursion
再帰呼び出し = saiki yobidashi = recursive call
関数 = kansū = function
基底条件 = kitei jōken = base case

Why the best solution works:
イ says that processing inside a function uses the function itself. That is the defining behavior of recursion.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Responding to events as they occur describes event-driven processing, not a function calling itself.

ウ:
Keeping a completed function in memory for later reuse describes retention, caching, or reuse. It does not create nested self-calls.

エ:
Returning to the state before a failed operation describes rollback or state restoration, not recursion.

Memory trick:
Recursion goes inward by self-calls until a base case; rollback goes backward after failure.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 再入可能プログラムの特徴はどれか。
questions.romaji: Sainyū kanō puroguramu no tokuchō wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which is a characteristic of a reentrant program?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 主記憶上のどこのアドレスに配置しても、実行することができる。
options.romaji: Shu kioku-jō no doko no adoresu ni haichi shite mo, jikkō suru koto ga dekiru.
options.en: It can execute at any main-memory address.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 手続の内部から自分自身を呼び出すことができる。
options.romaji: Tetsuzuki no naibu kara jibun jishin o yobidasu koto ga dekiru.
options.en: It can call itself from inside a procedure.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 必要な部分を補助記憶装置から読み込みながら動作する。
options.romaji: Hitsuyō na bubun o hojo kioku sōchi kara yomikominagara dōsa suru.
options.en: It runs while loading needed parts from auxiliary storage.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 複数のタスクからの呼び出しに対して、並行して実行されても、それぞれのタスクに正しい結果を返す。
options.romaji: Fukusū no tasuku kara no yobidashi ni taishite, heikō shite jikkō sarete mo, sorezore no tasuku ni tadashii kekka o kaesu.
options.en: Even when concurrently called by multiple tasks, it returns correct results to each.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Imagine the same vending-machine program serving two customers at almost the same time. A reentrant program keeps each customer's work separate, so one call does not overwrite another call's temporary state. Both callers receive the correct result even when their executions overlap.

Technical breakdown:
Reentrant code can be entered again before an earlier invocation has finished. It avoids unsafe shared mutable state or protects it, and keeps per-call state separate. Therefore multiple tasks can execute the same code concurrently without one invocation corrupting another. Reentrancy is about safe overlapping calls; recursion is about code calling itself.

Japanese keywords to remember:
再入可能 = sainyū kanō = reentrant
複数のタスク = fukusū no tasuku = multiple tasks
並行して実行 = heikō shite jikkō = execute concurrently
正しい結果 = tadashii kekka = correct result

Why the best solution works:
エ states the required property directly: concurrent calls from multiple tasks still return the correct independent result to each task.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Code that can run regardless of its memory address is relocatable code. Address independence is different from concurrent-call safety.

イ:
A procedure calling itself is recursion. Recursive code is not automatically reentrant, and reentrant code need not be recursive.

ウ:
Loading needed sections from auxiliary storage while running describes overlay or loading behavior used under memory limits, not reentrancy.

Memory trick:
Recursive = calls itself. Reentrant = multiple callers can safely be inside at once.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: Javaにおいて、よく使われる機能などを再利用できるようにコンポーネント化するための仕様はどれか。
questions.romaji: Java ni oite, yoku tsukawareru kinō nado o sairiyō dekiru yō ni konpōnento-ka suru tame no shiyō wa dore ka.
questions.en: In Java, which specification componentizes reusable functions?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
JavaBeans are reusable building blocks for Java programs. A developer can package a common feature as a component and use that component in different applications instead of rebuilding it each time. The question asks for the specification designed for that component model.

Technical breakdown:
A JavaBean follows Java component conventions so tools and programs can discover and reuse its properties and behavior. The key exam words are “componentize” and “reuse.” JavaScript is a language, while a Java application and an applet are kinds of programs rather than the reusable-component specification being asked for.

Japanese keywords to remember:
再利用 = sairiyō = reuse
コンポーネント化 = konpōnento-ka = componentization
仕様 = shiyō = specification
JavaBeans = JavaBeans = Java reusable components

Why the best solution works:
JavaBeans is specifically the Java specification for reusable software components, matching both clues in the question.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
JavaScript is a programming and scripting language commonly used for Web behavior. It is not Java's reusable-component specification.

ウ:
A Java application is a general program written in Java. It may use components, but “Java application” is not the component standard.

エ:
A Java applet is the historical model of a Java program downloaded to and run on a client. It describes deployment, not reusable componentization.

Memory trick:
Beans are ingredients you reuse; applications and applets are complete dishes.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: Web環境での動的処理を実現するプログラムであって、Webサーバ上だけで動作するものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Web kankyō de no dōteki shori o jitsugen suru puroguramu de atte, Web sāba-jō dake de dōsa suru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which dynamic Web program runs only on the Web server?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Web processing can happen in the browser or on the server. A servlet stays in the server's kitchen: it receives a request, performs processing there, and sends a response back. The client does not download the servlet to execute it.

Technical breakdown:
A Java servlet runs inside a servlet container on the Web server and implements server-side dynamic processing. In the historical FE context, JavaScript and VBScript represent browser/client-side scripts, while a Java applet is downloaded from a server and runs on the client. The phrase “Webサーバ上だけで動作” identifies the servlet.

Japanese keywords to remember:
Webサーバ = Web sāba = Web server
動的処理 = dōteki shori = dynamic processing
サーブレット = sāburetto = servlet
クライアント = kuraianto = client

Why the best solution works:
A Java servlet executes on the Web server, so it alone matches the stated execution location.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
JavaScript normally executes in the browser in this exam context, so it is client-side rather than server-only.

イ:
A Java applet is downloaded to the client and executed there, the opposite of server-only execution.

エ:
VBScript is treated as client-side scripting in this historical FE question, so it does not identify server-only processing.

Memory trick:
Servlet serves from the server; applet arrives at the client.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: コンパイル済みのオブジェクトコードがサーバに格納されていて、クライアントからの要求によってクライアントへ転送されて実行されるプログラムはどれか。
questions.romaji: Konpairu-zumi no obujekuto kōdo ga sāba ni kakunō sarete ite, kuraianto kara no yōkyū ni yotte kuraianto e tensō sarete jikkō sareru puroguramu wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which program is downloaded from a server and executed on the client?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
The question describes a small compiled program waiting on a server. When a user requests it, the program is downloaded to the user's machine and runs there. That historical Java delivery model is an applet.

Technical breakdown:
Follow the location clues:
1. The code is already compiled into object code.
2. It is stored on a server.
3. A client request transfers it to the client.
4. Execution happens on the client.
A Java applet fits all four clues. A servlet stays and runs on the server.

Japanese keywords to remember:
コンパイル済み = konpairu-zumi = compiled
オブジェクトコード = obujekuto kōdo = object code
転送 = tensō = transfer
クライアント = kuraianto = client

Why the best solution works:
An applet is compiled Java code that, in the historical model, is downloaded from a server and executed on the client.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
A servlet performs server-side processing. It is not transferred to the client for execution.

ウ:
A script is a general interpreted program concept and does not specifically match the compiled downloadable Java object-code model.

エ:
A thread is a unit or flow of execution inside a process. It is not a downloadable application type stored on a server.

Memory trick:
Applet downloads and runs at the client; servlet stays and runs at the server.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: HTML文書の文字の大きさ、文字の色、行間などの視覚表現の情報を扱う標準仕様はどれか。
questions.romaji: HTML bunsho no moji no ōkisa, moji no iro, gyōkan nado no shikaku hyōgen no jōhō o atsukau hyōjun shiyō wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which standard handles HTML visual presentation such as font size, color, and line spacing?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
HTML describes what a page contains, such as headings and paragraphs. CSS describes how those things look, such as their size, color, spacing, and layout. Keeping structure and appearance separate makes one style reusable across many pages.

Technical breakdown:
CSS means Cascading Style Sheets. Rules select HTML elements and assign presentation properties such as font-size, color, line-height, margins, and layout. The question lists visual presentation information, which is CSS's exact responsibility. The other choices concern content management, feed distribution, or collaborative editing.

Japanese keywords to remember:
視覚表現 = shikaku hyōgen = visual presentation
文字の大きさ = moji no ōkisa = font size
文字の色 = moji no iro = text color
行間 = gyōkan = line spacing

Why the best solution works:
CSS is the standard designed to control the presentation and styling of HTML documents independently from their structure.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
A CMS is a content management system used to create and manage site content. It is not the styling specification for HTML.

ウ:
RSS is a structured feed and syndication format used to distribute updates. It does not control page appearance.

エ:
A Wiki is a collaborative system whose pages can be edited by users. It is an application type, not a visual-style standard.

Memory trick:
HTML says what it is; CSS says how it looks.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: XMLの特徴として、最も適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: XML no tokuchō to shite, mottomo tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which is the most appropriate feature of XML?

options.label: ア
options.jp: XMLでは、HTMLに、Webページの表示性能の向上を主な目的とした機能を追加している。
options.romaji: XML dewa, HTML ni, Web pēji no hyōji seinō no kōjō o shuna mokuteki to shita kinō o tsuika shite iru.
options.en: XML adds HTML functions mainly to improve page display.

options.label: イ
options.jp: XMLでは、ネットワークを介した情報システム間のデータ交換を容易にするために、任意のタグを定義することができる。
options.romaji: XML dewa, nettowāku o kaishita jōhō shisutemu-kan no dēta kōkan o yōi ni suru tame ni, nin'i no tagu o teigi suru koto ga dekiru.
options.en: XML allows custom tags to ease data exchange between information systems.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: XMLで用いることができるスタイル言語は、HTMLと同じものである。
options.romaji: XML de mochiiru koto ga dekiru sutairu gengo wa, HTML to onaji mono de aru.
options.en: XML uses the same style language as HTML.

options.label: エ
options.jp: XMLは、SGMLを基に開発されたHTMLとは異なり、独自の仕様として開発された。
options.romaji: XML wa, SGML o moto ni kaihatsu sareta HTML to wa kotonari, dokuji no shiyō to shite kaihatsu sareta.
options.en: XML was developed independently unlike SGML-based HTML.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
XML is a way to label pieces of data with meaningful names. A bookstore might use <title> and <price>, while a school might use <student> and <score>. Because systems can define tags that match their data, they can exchange structured information more clearly.

Technical breakdown:
XML means Extensible Markup Language. “Extensible” means users or systems can define suitable tags rather than being limited to a fixed display vocabulary. XML focuses on describing data structure and meaning, making it useful for data exchange between systems. HTML primarily defines Web-document structure for presentation. Both XML and HTML are related to SGML; XML was not created as an unrelated independent specification.

Japanese keywords to remember:
任意のタグ = nin'i no tagu = arbitrary/custom tags
データ交換 = dēta kōkan = data exchange
情報システム間 = jōhō shisutemu-kan = between information systems
拡張可能 = kakuchō kanō = extensible

Why the best solution works:
イ identifies XML's central strength: defining meaningful custom tags to represent structured data for exchange between information systems.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
XML was not created mainly by adding display-performance features to HTML. XML describes structured data rather than improving page rendering.

ウ:
XML does not simply use the same style language as HTML. XML can use technologies such as XSL/XSLT; the statement is too broad and false.

エ:
XML was derived from SGML principles, as was HTML. It was not developed as a completely independent specification unrelated to SGML.

Memory trick:
HTML presents a page; XML explains and exchanges data with extensible tags.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: JavaScriptの非同期通信の機能を使うことによって、動的なユーザーインタフェースを画面全体の遷移を伴わずに実現する技術はどれか。
questions.romaji: JavaScript no hidōki tsūshin no kinō o tsukau koto ni yotte, dōteki na yūzā intāfeisu o gamen zentai no sen'i o tomonawazu ni jitsugen suru gijutsu wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which technology uses asynchronous JavaScript communication for dynamic UI without a full-page transition?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A traditional page request reloads the whole page, even if only one small area changes. Ajax lets JavaScript ask the server for data in the background. When the response arrives, JavaScript updates only the necessary part, so the interface feels faster and stays on the same page.

Technical breakdown:
Ajax stands for Asynchronous JavaScript and XML. “Asynchronous” means the browser can continue responding while communication happens rather than blocking for a full navigation. JavaScript sends a request, receives data, and updates part of the document. XML appears in the historical name, although modern Ajax may exchange other formats such as JSON. The FE clue is dynamic partial update without full-page transition.

Japanese keywords to remember:
非同期通信 = hidōki tsūshin = asynchronous communication
動的 = dōteki = dynamic
画面遷移 = gamen sen'i = page/screen transition
ユーザーインタフェース = yūzā intāfeisu = user interface

Why the best solution works:
Ajax combines background server communication with JavaScript-driven partial page updates, exactly matching the question's “without a full-page transition” condition.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
CSS controls visual presentation. It does not communicate asynchronously with a server or fetch new data.

ウ:
RSS is a feed format for distributing updated content. It is not the browser technique for partial interactive updates.

エ:
SNS means social networking service, a category of service rather than an asynchronous Web programming technique.

Memory trick:
Ajax asks in the background and adjusts one area of the page.

Correct answer: ア
